issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting instructions about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one section (lines describing the constructor) instructs to initialize a final Stock in the constructor (implying an instance-level final field), while a later section explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static. This contradiction (instance final vs static) will confuse students about whether stock should be an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static field shared across all instances.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and unify the specification: either (A) require a static final Stock shared across all saloons and show it initialized at declaration (and update the constructor instructions to not require initialization in the constructor), or (B) require an instance final Stock initialized in the constructor and remove the 'static' requirement. Update the UML, textual description, and examples to consistently reflect the chosen design.

issues.description: The UML and textual specification indicate acceptSupplyDelivery should be a public (+) static method, but the solution implements it as package-private static (no visibility modifier). This visibility mismatch (public expected vs package-private implemented) could confuse students about the intended API and may cause access issues depending on how tests or other code expect to call the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended visibility explicit and consistent: if the method should be part of the public API (as UML '+' indicates), declare it as public static in the specification and in implementations (public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(...)). Update the solution and any template guidance to use the public modifier.
